title: HyCMAx: Power-Efficient Hybrid CMOS-Memristor Based Approximate Dividers for Error-Resilient Applications
problem: Approximate computing traditionally uses CMOS technology; exploring hybrid CMOS-memristor approaches can yield further performance and power gains.
motivation: Error-resilient applications (multimedia, image processing, neural networks) can tolerate approximation. Memristor technology offers potential for superior power and area efficiency when combined with CMOS.
method: Hybrid CMOS-memristor approach for approximate circuit design. Proposes approximate subtractor then uses it to implement restoring divider in hybrid CMOS-memristor topology at 28nm CMOS node.
key_novelty: First exploration of hybrid CMOS-memristor approximate computing for divider circuits; demonstrates feasibility and benefits of memristor integration.
contributions: Demonstration of power/area gains from memristor integration
Evaluation in neural network and image processing contexts
limitations: Abstract only; no discussion of memristor latency/variability; error rate/accuracy impact not quantified; applicability limited to error-resilient workloads.
primary_theme: Hybrid CMOS-memristor approximate computing for power efficiency
